Subject: Amberline on-prem cluster: node classes, storage allocation & runbook questions

Hi Carlos / Amberline team,

Thanks again for taking the preflight call yesterday. To make the upcoming workshop productive, I wanted to capture a short list of cluster planning questions so we can lock down node profiles, storage topology, and the runbook scope ahead of the session. Quick answers will let us prepare a tailored ops-runbook and disk mapping.

Short background: we expect Redwood Private to run isolated customer clusters in your on-prem racks behind your VPC gateway. We're validating: control plane footprint, node pools (cpu/memory/ephemeral vs persistent), local NVMe caching strategy, and PV storage classes for reliability and retention.

Could you confirm the following items before our workshop?
- Primary workload mix (query/real-time chat vs background batching). Rough CPU / RAM per replica and p95 latency targets.
- Intended use of local NVMe: cache-only vs persistent local PVs.
- Preferred persistence layer: Rook/Ceph, external SAN, or cloud attach?
- Encryption & key management: will you provide KMS/HSM and are there KMIP endpoints?
- Backup / snapshot RTO/RPO expectations and retention windows (days).
- Rack inventory: number of servers planned for cluster, cores per server, local NVMe capacity per host.
- Network: top-of-rack egress bandwidth and whether we can rely on VLANs for tenant isolation.

I've attached a short intake checklist and a draft runbook template so you can see the fields we'll fill in at the workshop.

Attachments: amberline-initial-sprint-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Next steps: please reply with the above details by EOD Wednesday so we can prep. If you prefer, we can handle any missing items in the workshop on Dec 22.

Thanks,

Ben Carter

Ben / team,

Thanks — answers below inline. I'll forward the rack inventory tomorrow morning.

Workload: mix of real-time inference for search/autocomplete (about 60% of traffic) and periodic batch transfer jobs for nightly re-index (40%). For real-time we'll target p95 token latency under 250ms and want single-digit seconds cold-start for larger prompts. Typical replica size: 8 vCPU / 32GB RAM for CPU-bound worker pods; control plane will be dedicated.

NVMe: we'd prefer to use NVMe as a local cache for KV/prefix caching only — not as authoritative persistent storage. We can provide at least 2 x 3.2TB NVMe drives per host for caching.

Persistence: primary persistence will be on our SAN (Dell/Isilon) with iSCSI LUNs exposed to the cluster. We're evaluating Rook for object-tiering to the SAN for object snapshots but the SAN is the canonical copy.

Encryption/KMS: we have an internal KMS (HashiCorp Vault) with KMIP endpoints; HSM not available initially.

Retention: snapshots daily, retention 30 days for index data; longer retention for audit logs (90 days). RTO target for inference nodes is 2 hours to recover at degraded capacity.

Rack inventory: I'll attach a CSV tomorrow with server counts and network capacity. To be specific today: 24 hosts initially, 10Gb top-of-rack uplinks, dual 25Gb NICs on hosts.

Network: VLAN segmentation OK, and we can set up an isolated management VLAN for control plane. Egress to cloud services restricted by proxy.

Questions for Redwood: for Cache-only NVMe, what eviction policy / KV cache size do you recommend? Also confirm recommended PVC reclaim policy for ephemeral vs persistent workloads.

Regards,
Carlos Vega
Platform Lead, Amberline Logistics
c.vega@amberline.com

Subject: Re: Amberline on-prem cluster: node classes, storage allocation & runbook questions

Carlos — perfect, that's very helpful. A few recommendations and answers to your questions:

1) Node pools / sizing
- Control plane: 3 control nodes (dedicated), 16 vCPU / 64GB recommended to handle k8s control loops and operator overhead.
- Inference workers (real-time): nodeclass-rt: 8vCPU / 64GB, local NVMe for KV/prefix cache. Start with 12 replicas across 24 hosts (spread by daemonset affinity) to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
- Batch workers: nodeclass-batch: 4vCPU / 16-32GB, tolerates preemption / scaled down at night.

2) NVMe as cache
- Cache-only approach is correct. We'll mount NVMe as a local PersistentVolume using local-storage provisioner and apply a reclaimPolicy: Delete for cache volumes. We recommend LRU eviction at application layer; Redwood's runtime will cap KV cache per replica to avoid full-disk issues (configurable, default 500GB per host).

3) Persistent storage
- Given SAN is canonical, use a StorageClass that binds to iSCSI-backed PVs (reclaimPolicy: Retain for critical indexes). For object-tiering or blob attachments, Rook/Ceph as a secondary tier is fine but ensure we have network QoS for Ceph traffic.

4) Encryption/KMS
- We'll integrate with HashiCorp Vault for envelope encryption. Need KMIP endpoint details and a service account with rotate keys permission. We'll stub the KMS config in the runbook.

5) Snapshots and retention
- Daily snapshots (automated) and 30-day retention for indexes is standard; we'll also stage weekly snapshots to an external archive for 90-day audit retention.

6) PVC reclaim policy recommendations
- Ephemeral / cache PVs: reclaimPolicy=Delete.
- Persistent indexes: reclaimPolicy=Retain with explicit admin process for cleanup.

Next steps:
- Irene / Neha — can you prepare a preflight test list (node provisioning, nvme health, iSCSI latency test, snapshot restore run) and a draft runbook for the workshop?
- Carlos — send the rack CSV and we'll annotate the runbook with exact host counts.

I've attached a short Redwood runbook template to show the sections we'll fill at the workshop. If Dec 22 works for your staff, I'll send a calendar invite with a pre-read.

Attachments: redwood-runbook-template.md (markdown)

Thanks,

Ben / Neha / Marissa,

I'll take point on the preflight checklist and the runbook sections for provisioning and validation. Draft plan below — I'll convert to PDF and attach.

Preflight / validation items (high priority):
- Hardware inventory verification (serials, firmware versions)
- NVMe health scan and SMART baseline on all hosts
- iSCSI latency and throughput synthetic tests (p95 under 10ms for index paths)
- Network VLAN isolation verification and MTU checks
- KMS integration smoke test (Vault KMIP endpoint connectivity)
- Snapshot restore dry-run to a staging namespace

Runbook sections to prepare for workshop:
- Cluster layout & nodeclass mapping (control / rt / batch)
- Storage classes and PV reclaim policy mapping
- Backup / snapshot flow and escalation path
- Failure recovery playbooks (node loss, PV corruption, storage array failover)
- Security checklist (access controls, firewall rules, logging endpoints)

I'll attach the preflight checklist as a PDF and will put time estimates against each test. Plan to have the draft to share by EOD Friday so Ben can include it in the Dec 22 invite.

Irene
